references.text: David asks God to examine his heart to reveal any hidden sins or thoughts, which reflects Jesus' ability to know people's thoughts and hearts.
Proverbs speaks of the Lord testing hearts, reflecting Jesus' knowledge of human hearts.
Jesus knows people's thoughts, a direct parallel to the event in Matthew 9:4.
Jesus asks the Pharisees a similar question about why they are thinking evil thoughts, showing his ability to know their innermost being.
Again, Jesus demonstrates his ability to understand people's thoughts and motives, paralleling the event in Matthew 9.
Jesus knows the disciples' thoughts, showing his divine insight into the human heart.
Acts refers to the prayer that God knows everyone's hearts, which aligns with Jesus' ability to see people's inner thoughts and motives.
Hebrews speaks of God's word as sharper than any double-edged sword, revealing the thoughts and intentions of the heart, paralleling Jesus' ability to know the human heart.
